lines.say: One page. 101 trips to your database, where your app keeps its data. Two trips would do.
lines.show: One page. [101 trips] to your database, where your app keeps its data. *Two trips* would do.

lines.say: Your code fetches 100 orders, then asks the database for each order's customer name, one at a time.
lines.show: Your code fetches 100 orders, then asks the database for each order's customer name, [one at a time.]

lines.say: That's the N plus 1 problem. N is the number of orders, plus one request for the list.
lines.show: That's the [N+1 problem.] *N* is the number of orders, plus *one* request for the list.

lines.say: Like getting a shopping list, then making a separate trip to the shop for every item.
lines.show: Like getting a shopping list, then making a [separate trip] to the shop for *every item.*

lines.say: The fix: ask for all the names together, in one request, or in the same request as the orders.
lines.show: The fix: ask for [all the names together,] in one request, or in the *same request* as the orders.

lines.say: Even AI-written code does this. So check how many database requests each page makes.
